page: Amazon Web Services m8gd.24xlarge is a general-purpose server instance powered by AWS Graviton processors. Built on the ARM64 architecture using the ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 core design, the instance features 96 dedicated physical cores operating at 2.8 GHz with a single thread per core. It is equipped with 384.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB per core. For local storage, the instance includes 5700 GB of NVMe SSD instance store volumes. Networking capabilities are anchored by a 40 Gbps baseline bandwidth managed via the AWS Nitro hypervisor.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core CPU and Geekbench multi-core scores placing in the top 10% of tested systems. Memory bandwidth is a notable strength, registering top-tier results for both cached small-block reads and uncached large-block reads and writes. The instance also demonstrates high throughput in database operations, static web serving, and Redis SET operations, which reached 198.92 million operations per second. However, single-core performance is more moderate, with stress-ng single-core and gzip compression benchmarks falling into the average tier.

The m8gd.24xlarge offers high resource density and qualitative cost efficiency for multi-threaded workloads due to its 96 dedicated physical cores and integrated high-capacity NVMe storage. This hardware profile eliminates the need for external storage attachments for data-heavy operations, though the ephemeral nature of instance store volumes represents a key operational tradeoff. While the instance excels at medium and large LLM text generation, it exhibits weaker performance in small-model text generation. It is highly suited for large-scale database deployments, multi-threaded software compilation, high-throughput web serving, and parallel data processing tasks.
